review_evidence: README identifies Specimen as a Lean testing/verification tool that derives generators, enumerators and checkers for inductive relations, inspired by QuickChick and formal testing literature.
The 118 current-primary files include the derivation engine plus extensive test/examples for STLC, permutations, regex matching, BST/balanced trees, Cedar policies and arithmetic compilers.

Inspected SpecimenTest.lean and DerivePermutationGenerator.lean: the test tree owns formal definitions/specifications and elaborated derive/guard examples rather than mere runner glue, so test-labelled material is retained. Package configuration is lakefile.toml and non-primary.
summary: Retain Specimen’s derivation machinery and its substantive formal test/example corpus; no safe primary exclusion was established.

review_evidence: Ran `grep -cE '\b(theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom)\b'` over all 24 files; 21 had nonzero matches (range 2-181), 3 had zero matches.
Read Specimen.lean in full (878 bytes, 25 lines): a bare `import Specimen.<Module>` list under a header comment identifying it as the library root; no open/declaration content.

Read SpecimenTest.lean in full (5710 bytes, ~140 lines): a bare `import SpecimenTest.<Module>` list grouped by section comments identifying it as the test-suite root; no open/declaration content beyond imports and comments.

Read SpecimenTest/DeriveArbitrarySuchThat/SimultaneousMatchingTests.lean in full (1275 bytes, 37 lines): contains `open Plausible`, `open ArbitrarySizedSuchThat`, two `set_option` commands, and five `#guard_msgs(drop info) in derive_generator (...)` executable test invocations -- genuine content, not a pure import file, and correctly retained (not excluded) regardless.

Spot-checked Specimen/DeriveConstrainedProducer.lean (163733 bytes, 2863 lines): opens with 15 imports, `open Lean Elab Command Meta Term Parser` / `open Idents Schedules ProofWidgets`, then substantial `def` content (e.g. `mkInitialUnknownMap`, `mkProducerInitialUnifyState`) with docstrings citing POPL '18 and QuickChick provenance.

Spot-checked Specimen/Scoring.lean (79893 bytes, 1749 lines): a `namespace Scoring` module with an extensive module-doc comment describing the Scorable typeclass, ScorerBundle, and scoring-layer architecture, followed by real typeclass/def content.

Spot-checked Specimen/DeriveSchedules.lean (81050 bytes, 1484 lines): a `namespace Schedules` module with a module-doc comment describing PreScheduleStep/ScheduleStep/ScheduleEnv/SCC-decomposition concepts, followed by real def content adapted from QuickChick's scheduling algorithm.
summary: Ran the declaration-keyword grep across all 24 changed/added files and read the three zero-match files in full to confirm their disposition. Specimen.lean and SpecimenTest.lean are pure `import`-only aggregators (root library module and root test module respectively; no `open`, notation, or declarations of their own) and are retained as navigation data per FILTER-007. SpecimenTest/DeriveArbitrarySuchThat/SimultaneousMatchingTests.lean is not a pure import file despite the zero grep count: it contains `open Plausible`/`open ArbitrarySizedSuchThat`, `set_option` commands, and five executable `derive_generator (...)` macro invocations under `#guard_msgs` -- genuine formal content the theorem/lemma/def keyword list does not capture. Spot-checked the three largest non-zero-match files (Specimen/DeriveConstrainedProducer.lean 163733 bytes/2863 lines, Specimen/DeriveSchedules.lean 81050 bytes/1484 lines, Specimen/Scoring.lean 79893 bytes/1749 lines): all are substantial working Lean derivation-machinery modules with real `def`/typeclass/namespace content and module-doc comments, consistent with the prior review's characterization of this unit as Specimen's derivation machinery and formal test/example corpus. No file in this unit matches a documented exclusion pattern (pure-import files are retained per FILTER-007, not excluded). All 24 files stay searchable.
